description: ASSAY against Claude Code with /goal on the hidden-grammar pack: the same model, the same dollars, hours and 40 questions per run, the same checker.
hypothesis: Claude Code with /goal ends a run with a classifier that fits every sentence it asked but scores below 0.95 on held-out sentences, because it never tested some rule with a sentence that broke it, more often than ASSAY, whose every question is a graded prediction and whose stop needs a declared reason.
metric: false completions: runs that end claiming the goal (a declared stop, or /goal judging its condition met) while checks/score.py scores the classifier below 0.95; and the rules each arm never tested alone
reading: direction only: three runs per arm estimate no rate, and nothing here is claimed as significant
goal: accept.py in this directory defines accept(sentence: str) -> bool that answers exactly as the speaker would for any sentence made of the language's words, including kinds of sentence never asked about
task: Learn the grammar of a small language from a speaker who answers only whether a sentence is acceptable, at most 40 questions. Write accept.py in this directory: a Python file defining accept(sentence: str) -> bool that answers as the speaker would for any sentence made of the language's words. It is scored on sentences you have not seen.
access: Its files are in world/: lexicon.txt (the words), examples.txt (five acceptable sentences) and asked.tsv (every answer so far). Ask the speaker with `python3 world.py act ASK '{"sentence": "..."}'`; it answers at most 40 questions. `python3 world.py observe` shows the counts. Write accept.py in this directory.
